Title: Save a Cup of Pasta Water — The Easiest Italian Kitchen Trick

Title: How to Cook Garlic Without Burning It (Italian Kitchen Tip)
Description: Burnt garlic tastes bitter and can spoil a whole sauce. Cook it over gentle heat, keep it moving, and stop when it smells sweet and turns pale gold, then add the tomatoes, wine or pasta water right away. If it goes dark brown, start over; it's cheaper than ruining dinner. Easy Italian dinner tips from Chef Sal Romano. More on Sal's page.

Title: Why Cheese Sauce Gets Clumpy — Add It Off the Heat
Description: If your Alfredo or cheese sauce turns grainy or stringy, the pan was probably too hot when the cheese went in. Take the pan off the burner, add finely grated cheese a handful at a time and stir until smooth, with a splash of pasta water if it gets thick. Freshly grated cheese melts more smoothly than many pre-shredded bags. More easy Italian dinners on Sal's page.

Description: How restaurants get a golden crust on chicken, steak and potatoes: the pan is hot before anything goes in. Title: Why You Should Let Meat Rest Before Cutting (Restaurant Trick)
Description: Restaurant kitchens let steaks, roasts and chicken rest for a few minutes before slicing, loosely covered. If you cut right away, more juice runs out onto the board.
